title: Make.com Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits and Real Costs
summary: Make.com pricing includes Free, Team, and Business plans. Review each tier's monthly costs, operation limits, and features to choose the right plan.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits if Make's metering is the problem


If per-step charges dominate your bill, or you need to run the automation engine on your own infrastructure, Activepieces is worth testing: its core is MIT-licensed and self-hostable, with 740 integrations in the open source monorepo.


Otherwise Make's metering is usually workable once you have priced it.


### How execution steps consume credits


Take a scenario with a router, an iterator and six API calls. Make counts each module execution, so it spends credits on every one of them.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/polling-vs-webhooks-for-integration-triggers-in-2026) doesn't meter steps at all: flows are unlimited on every plan and credits meter AI usage. The practical effect is that a long chain of non-AI steps consumes no credits there, where that same scenario spends a credit on every module execution on Make.


The Free plan is $0 with 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows, Plus is $20 a month and Team is $200, all listed on the Activepieces pricing page, so upgrading from free to Plus costs $20 per month.


The table below sets the two side by side. Read the credit-meter row first, because the entry price and credit allowance mean nothing until you know what one credit buys.


Make Activepieces


Entry price $12 $20


Included credits 10,000 1,000 a month on Free


What a credit meters Each module execution AI usage


Self-hosting No; Make runs in its own cloud Yes, through the open-source edition


Where Make is stronger Mature routing, error handling and a broad module catalogue Younger tooling; the gain is cost predictability


If your flows are short, the $20 Activepieces entry price against Make's $9 buys nothing, since a three-step scenario costs only three Make credits per run.


It pays off only where step count's what inflates your Make bill, as with the 800-credit iterator run above, which consumes no credits on Activepieces unless it contains AI steps.


Don't expect self-hosting to remove the bill; it changes it. You stop paying per run, but you take on servers, upgrades, backups and uptime, and someone on your team now owns them.


### Rebuilding one scenario as a test


Take the module-by-module price you already worked out for your heaviest scenario and rebuild only that one in Activepieces, after checking its connectors against the 740 integrations in the open source monorepo, ensuring you won't be blocked by missing connectors.


Don't migrate everything on the strength of a pricing page.


Then, in order:


1. Run it against the same inputs for a representative week.
2. Count the credits its AI steps use.
3. Compare the total with the credits Make consumed.


Watch where the rebuild fights you. A router with nested conditions, a custom error path or a connector that exists in Make but not here will cost engineering hours, and those hours belong in the comparison.


If the rebuild is cheaper and behaves the same, you have a reason to move. If it's roughly equal, Make's tooling depth's likely worth keeping.
